This might help me later, but I think it's a good question for discussion. In previous conversations, I've discovered there can be very different ideas between users about what a moderator should and should not be like and do. So I thought it would be good as a topic of discussion here.

How do you think moderators should behave, and what do you expect from them?
What do you want from moderators?

I think moderators should stick to their titles and be moderate. Remove flame wars, harassment, and toxic trolling. Remove spam and encourage posting of relevant content. Curate a sub when the voting system fails. And do all of that without becoming corrupt and abusing power. Engage the community seeking feedback and following their lead on things. It's a public servant role, not a dictatorship, and not a simple human spam filter. The role of a moderator is to maintain the functionality and usefulness of a sub or community for the purpose it was intended or the purpose the community would like to use it for. It requires common sense, responsibility, accountability, some creativity, and a community that is engaged along with the mod in collective stewardship of the community, ideally.

Personally, I want moderators to uphold the laws they are supposed to uphold without letting anything personal get in between that.

Also, I don't want every law to be upheld every time. We are not brain dead, we are not robots and we are not children. Sometimes logic can be upheld in the face of ignorant protocol. If something seems acceptable as an exception to the rule, then make it an exception to the rule. Again, you're not brain dead or a robot. If something in a vote based system has managed to become popular despite being against the rules, don't remove it based on rule #3.52, stick the rule book up your ass and let the people speak for themselves.

Thirdly, stop acting like we should all feel sorry for you and worship you based on your 'volunteer' status. You CHOSE to do what you do for whatever strange reason. I'm not going to respect you automatically for that. What makes me respect you is if I can level with you man to man or avatar to avatar and sort something out.
Moderators should behave like janitors. Not like kings.

I think the moderator(s) of /v/AskVoat follow your ideals.

I would say it depends on the sub. Some subs like /r/AskHistorians are excellent because of absolutely strict moderation and removal of anything less than a comprehensive, sourced answer. Other subs are excellent because of a more laissez-faire approach, allowing the community to decide what is or isn't appropriate.

Ultimately, I think moderators need to be active users, and engage with the community they're moderating. If content is removed or a user is banned, they need to be able to give a solid reason why, and enforce those rules consistently.

One of the key duties of the moderators is to ensure the community achieves its purpose by preventing content that is too easily digestible from taking over the whole site. One example is memes - far too many sites have been destroyed by them. If the purpose of a subverse is to encourage fruitful discussion, than mod needs to make the call that the subverse would be better without memes than with memes and hence ban them (perhaps run a monthly memes thread if they have to). I'm not against subverses designed to share memes - I'm against subverses becoming pretty much completely memes.
